blocks.path: Eyelid problems
s: Find out what to do if you have a lump on your eyelid, or an eyelid that's swollen, sticky, itchy or painful.

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Most eyelid problems are harmless
s: Many eyelid problems are not serious.

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Most eyelid problems are harmless
s: It's fairly common to have any of these problems:

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Most eyelid problems are harmless
s: a lump that goes away by itself after several days or weeks

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Most eyelid problems are harmless
s: mildly itchy, flaky or sticky eyelids that clear up by themselves

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Most eyelid problems are harmless
s: swelling from a nearby insect bite, injury or operation that goes away after a week or so

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Most eyelid problems are harmless
s: twitching or blinking from time to time – often when you're tired

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Most eyelid problems are harmless
s: eyelids that droop (or get more "hooded") as you get older

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: Your symptoms might give you an idea of what's causing your eyelid problem.
But do not self-diagnose – see a pharmacist, GP or optician.

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: Eyelid problem | Possible cause

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: Lump or swelling on eyelid | Stye or meibomian cyst (chalazion)

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: Itchy, flaky, sticky or swollen eyelid | Allergy, blepharitis, or conjunctivitis

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: Yellow lump or patch on eyelid | Xanthelasma (yellow patches sometimes caused by high cholesterol)

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: Eyelid turning outwards or inwards | Ectropion or entropion

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: Hot, painful and swollen eyelid | Cellulitis

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Types of eyelid problems
s: There is separate information about twitching eyelids.

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > A pharmacist can help with eyelid problems
s: You can ask a pharmacist about:

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > A pharmacist can help with eyelid problems
s: what you can do to treat common eyelid problems, like a stye or conjunctivitis, yourself

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > A pharmacist can help with eyelid problems
s: if you can buy anything to help – for example, cleaning solutions for sticky eyelids

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > A pharmacist can help with eyelid problems
s: if you need to see an optician or GP

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you're worried about an eyelid problem

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: your eyelid symptoms are not improving or they're lasting a long time

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have yellow lumps or patches around your eyes

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: your swollen eyelid is red, hot, painful, tender or blistered

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: your eyelid droops suddenly

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you cannot open your eye or keep it open

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: the pain is in your eye (not your eyelid)

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: the white of your eye is very red, in part or all over

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have eye symptoms and a headache or you feel sick or are being sick

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: a newborn baby (less than 1 month old) has a sticky, red eye

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you're sensitive to light (photophobia)

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: your eyesight changes – for example, you have blurred vision and see wavy flashing lights, zigzag patterns or coloured spots or lines

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have a very high temperature, feel hot, cold or shivery, or you feel generally unwell

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you think it's an allergic reaction

blocks.path: Eyelid problems > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP or optician appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.
